observation.description: The packaged SnapbackAssetClient (@expo/snapback-client/assets — the guide's 'framework-neutral upload task is client.assets.start') builds its own raw fetches for attempt creation, TUS HEAD/PATCH, and finalize with only content-type plus an optional x-snapback-dev-user header. It never carries the wrapped client's bearer or the x-snapback-auth-client-protocol offer, so on a sessions-mode server every upload fails at attempt creation with SNAPBACK_AUTH_PROFILE_CLIENT_UNSUPPORTED. The client is dev-mode-only in practice. The same lifecycle succeeds when driven with authenticated raw requests (this arm's A1-04), so the server side is fine.

competitorOutcome.description: Firebase's Storage SDK carries the signed-in user's auth on every upload transparently; an upload surface that cannot authenticate is below the frozen bar for any provider.

mustNotRegress: The task-store hygiene (no bearer/staging material persisted in resume facts) — fix the request headers, not the persisted-fact set.
smallestCoherentFix: Route SnapbackAssetClient requests through the wrapped client's authenticated transport (bearer + protocol offers), keeping x-snapback-dev-user for dev custody, with a sessions-mode packaged-closure upload conformance test.
acceptanceWitness: createAssetClient(sessionsClient).start(...) reaches status 'ready' against a sessions-mode local server on the public closure.
